hypotheses: JQ1-S inhibits BRD4, displacing it from acetylated chromatin and causing global loss of H3K9ac and H3K14ac, which may indirectly reduce H3K79 methylation and increase H3K79me0.
JQ1-S may inhibit DOT1L indirectly through BRD4-dependent transcription of DOT1L or its cofactors, leading to reduced H3K79me1 and accumulation of H3K79me0.
JQ1-S may alter H3K56 acetylation or methylation states via BRD4-dependent regulation of histone acetyltransferases or deacetylases, contributing to the observed H3K56me0 increase.

The histone mark changes may reflect a general stress response or cell cycle arrest rather than direct bromodomain inhibition, as suggested by the mixed pattern of acetylation and methylation changes.

Donor compounds with similar anchor similarity (e.g., decitabine, zebularine, methylstat) may share epigenetic mechanisms that produce comparable histone mark profiles, but their pharmacological classes differ from JQ1-S.
object.evidence_gap: No direct evidence links JQ1-S to the specific histone mark changes (H3K79me0, H3K56me0, H3K79me1, H3K9ac1K14ac0, H3K27me0K36me2, H3K9me0K14ac1) in A375 cells at 1 µM for 24 hours. The donor descriptions are needed to assess whether any donor has known effects on these marks, and to determine if the observed changes are consistent with bromodomain inhibition or other mechanisms.
